headline: High: Dify can write and egress broadly while LlamaFactory is read-only/offline, creating prompt-injection and data-handling risk mainly through Dify’s shared datastore and tool wiring.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge base files and wire tools into agent/workflow apps, while LlamaFactory has no filesystem or network surfaces. The pair still has a plausible injection path if Dify content is later reused as instructions, but the bridge is not explicit and is weaker than a shared filesystem/MCP case.
conditions: IF Dify ingests attacker-controlled knowledge base content and later reuses it as instructions
IF an operator manually copies Dify output into a downstream prompt without sanitization
mitigations: Add a prompt-injection filter to uploaded KB content
Separate instruction text from retrieved documents in Dify
Require human review before reusing Dify outputs
Use a fixed system prompt that ignores quoted instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for retrieved snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs and has broad network egress, but LlamaFactory has no filesystem read/write, no network egress, and no data classes touched. Leakage from Dify to LlamaFactory is therefore limited; the main risk is operator-mediated copying rather than an automatic shared workspace.
conditions: IF an operator pastes Dify conversation logs into LlamaFactory training or support workflows
IF Dify exports knowledge base content into a shared external system
mitigations: Avoid copying conversation logs into LlamaFactory
Redact secrets from Dify outputs before reuse
Restrict Dify exports to approved datasets
Confirm LlamaFactory remains offline-only
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on export

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify can write the filesystem and run shell/subprocesses, while LlamaFactory is non-runnable and has no write or shell capabilities. There is no direct write-write conflict between the pair, so only limited contention exists through operator-managed shared resources, not a default capability clash.
conditions: IF both are pointed at the same mutable directory through external orchestration
IF an operator manually synchronizes artifacts between Dify and another writable system
mitigations: Keep Dify and LlamaFactory on separate workspaces
Disable shared mutable mounts
Run Dify jobs serially when touching the same artifacts
Document ownership of generated files
requires-engineering: add locking around shared storage

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can produce tool-using agent outputs, and LlamaFactory is a customer-support system with no verification or action-taking controls shown. If Dify output is forwarded into LlamaFactory workflows, the latter may treat it as authoritative support content, creating a default cascading-error path even though the exact integration is undocumented.
conditions: IF Dify-generated text is used as source material for LlamaFactory responses
IF LlamaFactory operators do not add a verification step before publishing answers
mitigations: Require human approval for support replies sourced from Dify
Mark Dify output as untrusted in downstream prompts
Add citation checks before publishing
Limit Dify to draft-only generation
requires-engineering: build a verification gate between systems

E_compliance.rationale: Dify handles conversation logs and knowledge base content, while LlamaFactory lists no data classes or retention/residency controls. The pair therefore has a compliance gap only if regulated data is routed from Dify into LlamaFactory workflows; the other agent is not cited because it exposes no relevant compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from Dify is exported into LlamaFactory processes
IF retention or deletion obligations apply to Dify conversation logs
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into LlamaFactory
Classify Dify logs before export
Set short retention on Dify conversation logs
Review vendor residency for any exported dataset
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows
